title: Playlists empty after reconnecting storage.
body:
### This issue respects the following points:

- [X] This is a **bug**, not a question or a configuration issue; Please visit our forum or chat rooms first to troubleshoot with volunteers, before creating a report. The links can be found [here](https://jellyfin.org/contact/).
- [X] This issue is **not** already reported on [GitHub](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue) _(I've searched it)_.
- [X] I'm using an up to date version of Jellyfin Server stable, unstable or master; We generally do not support previous older versions. If possible, please update to the latest version before opening an issue.
- [X] I agree to follow Jellyfin's [Code of Conduct](https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/community-standards.html#code-of-conduct).
- [X] This report addresses only a single issue; If you encounter multiple issues, kindly create separate reports for each one.

### Description of the bug

Earlier today, my playlists were perfectly intact. Now they are completely empty.

### Reproduction steps

This has happened twice. I've updated since the first time it happened. I run the docker version, it appears to happen when my rclone mount fails, and persists even when I restore the directory.

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

The playlists remain completely empty, but should restore once the drive is reconnected.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

My playlists persisting.

### Jellyfin Server version

Older*

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Happens to me too. I disconnect my USB to add some music from my laptop, then when I reconnect it the playlists are completely empty. Pretty annoying that it completely purges the songs from the .xml file instead of just giving me errors or whatever.

comments.author: Shadowghost
comments.body:
Jellyfin does not know if a disconnected drive means "data is gone" or "intentionally disconnected". We opted for assuming that the data is gone since that's exactly what happens from an application point of view. Main reason for cleaning up the playlist in those cases is that otherwise they don't play or randomly fail because the media you try to access is not there.

TLDR: This is intentional behavior as of now. It might change with the DB rewrite and having proper foreign keyes but this is still (far) in the future.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@Shadowghost Would the DB rewrite change how playlist items are stored? As of right now, the playlist items are coupled to the media paths, meaning every time I move media files to a different path or replace media files (and playlists are then cleaned up), the associated playlist entry gets deleted.

The way playlists currently work that's expected behaviour I suppose, which makes opening another issue moot. But I'm definitely not the only one with this issue (#12501, and several forum threads). This behaviour makes playlists in the current state unusable for myself and my users.

I'd open a feature request, however it's unlikely to get traction, as there's a multitude of open issues regarding playlists on the feature tracker - some of them already resolved, multitudes of duplicates and almost none of them are relevant to the way the server handles playlists imo.

Would love to get some insight. Thank you all for your hard work on improving Jellyfin!

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Jellyfin does not know if a disconnected drive means "data is gone" or "intentionally disconnected". We opted for assuming that the data is gone since that's exactly what happens from an application point of view. Main reason for cleaning up the playlist in those cases is that otherwise they don't play or randomly fail because the media you try to access is not there.
> 
> TLDR: This is intentional behavior as of now. It might change with the DB rewrite and having proper foreign keyes but this is still (far) in the future.

Thanks for your response and your work on jellyfin! :)
When the missing files are returned, why would it not automatically re-add them to the playlist though? (or leave the removed media in the playlist, hide it from the user but just return an error until the media is returned/found)

comments.author: Shadowghost
comments.body:
> When the missing files are returned, why would it not automatically re-add them to the playlist though? (or leave the removed media in the playlist, hide it from the user but just return an error until the media is returned/found)

Because we do not soft-delete items if they are missing on the file system. Once removed, Jellyfin removed any metadata associated with the files, so there is no way we can magically know if a newly added (or re-added) file was part of a Collection/Playlist/etc. before

comments.author: reporter

> You can already achieve that by manually removing the trigger for that scheduled task via the UI

Thank you! - For anyone looking in the future, it's at dashboard -> scheduled tasks -> Clean up collections and playlists. The default trigger is "on application startup" and it looks like you can just delete that task. :)

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Hey guys, is there a way to recover the playlists from a backup?
I've tried copying the backed up xml files back over and rescanned, but the playlists remain empty.

Edit:
Ok, just had success.

Delete everything in the /data/playlists folder
Manually remove each of the playlists from the jellyfin UI
Restart the jellyfin server / container (probably obsolete)
Scan libraries (probably obsolete)
Stop the jellyfin server / container
Copy the back ups into /data/playlists - the folder will be the name of the playlist and there will be a file called "playlist.xml" inside.
Start the jellyfin server / container
Rescan libraries

Hopefully this will help someone.

And then delete the task per reporter's comment above

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
@participant4 mostly worked with a caveat for me.

This is on a Windows box so not sure if it's different elsewhere.

Stop the Jellyfin service.
Delete the offending playlist folders in c\programdata\jellyfin\data\playlists

I couldn't delete the playlists, just kept getting errors so I had to then...

Browse the DB c\programdata\jellyfin\data\jellyfin.db, open the database of TypeBaseItems (You can use DB Browser for SQLLite for this on Windows)
Filter Type as : **MediaBrowser.Controller.Playlists.Playlist**
In there you will see your playlists (and yes they have the individual songs/items stored in the DB too).  My issue was the playlists were empty in both the XML & the Database.  If the playlist still exists in the database copying the XML file back does not fix the issue since the DB seems to rule supreme.

Here is a sample of the DB showing the songs/items in there.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/170f0529-e71c-4c1f-8917-e99a7f490866)

Delete the offending rows in the database.  Save/close the DB.
Copy the backup playlist folders back in to c\programdata\jellyfin\data\playlists
Start the service
Scan all libraries

This seems to then populate the DB properly again.

I'm really not sure on the thought process on the task running right at startup.  I understand wanting to clean up when files go away but maybe delay this 30 seconds or something so that anyone with network storage that maybe hasn't connected/spun up yet doesn't get bit.

One thing I ran into  - 

I had to restore from an older backup of the playlists and had some issues like you described.. 

I finally deleted the playlists.. created new ones with the same name. (with maybe a single song each)

I opened up the XML and there is a userid value that had changed since the original xml backups were made..   I plugged that ID into my backup versions of the xml, copied them to the playlists folders and did the restart/ rescan stuff..

comments.author: participant19
comments.body:
> Jellyfin does not know if a disconnected drive means "data is gone" or "intentionally disconnected". We opted for assuming that the data is gone since that's exactly what happens from an application point of view. Main reason for cleaning up the playlist in those cases is that otherwise they don't play or randomly fail because the media you try to access is not there.
> 
> TLDR: This is intentional behavior as of now. It might change with the DB rewrite and having proper foreign keyes but this is still (far) in the future.

This is a very aggressive and dissapointing policy to implement. It results in extremely frustrating and permanent data loss, making Jellyfin fragile. As a user, I would rather take a few error messages or skipped songs over having many hours of curation be suddenly and permanently deleted without warning.

It makes me worried of what other fragile policies are hiding elsewhere in the software?

comments.author: Shadowghost
participant20
comments.body:
> Just to stop all the whining here about needing to disable a scheduled task to fix this problem or having stable storage availability (which frankly is the core issue here):

Show some common basic respect to people! There is no need to start calling people as whiners and inexpert. If someone say something you don't like, don't start calling them with names or demanding them to do something else. 

The core problem is that the playlists and collections are handled improperly, illogically, and data destructive manner.
The part of the core problems is that **default** setting is such that _data destruction occurs_. 
Something that shouldn't happen in first place at all.
And there is many other reasons why suddenly a storage availability doesn't exist anymore, others than just how stable someone has storage in their hardware. As Jellyfin will glitch sometimes, and erase its playlists and collections as it loses the library, that is absolutely constantly available and functional to all other services on the server and to all other containers etc.
Luckily library database isn't affected, but the playlists and collections seems to be. 

The playlists and the collections should be handled like any common media playlist or collections for decades.
A separate file where the data location is saved. 
That file doesn't get any data in it removed by default unless user so commands.
That playlist is always then dynamically stored, if the source for the data is available or not, it is irrelevant, as the data in playlist always points to the source. If the data is not available, then the playlist item is marked as "not available".
Handling it like .m3u playlist. 
If user has lot of items "not available" in playlist, but not all, because deleting the source data or not having it mounted means user will get the idea that some are available but not all. If none is available, it signals the user that something else is wrong. The user needs to initiate the playlist / collection refresh or update. Where the data is checked does the source exist or not, and if not, then remove it from the playlist. But that is _always_ user initiated action with an warning.

> if you're so knowledgeable I dare you to just fix it yourself the next time instead of complaining about the work people do for you for free at their own expense.

Stop that kind behavior with attack to person. If someone can't take the critique, then better stop being in F/OSS communities all together.
The most important part in the F/OSS is that users can report and give feedback of the software that they are using. That is the cornerstone of the whole process. Anyone who wants to participate to improve the software, doesn't need to even know programming etc. Demanding that specific person should fix something as they so request, is not correct in the whole spirit of the F/OSS. 

So how about recognizing that the problem is its default behavior, and the overall behavior to handle the playlists and collections incorrectly at the moment, and has been problem for long time, and is good thing that it gets changed?
